scaleInfo.name: Harmonic Minor Scale
scaleInfo.character: Exotic, dramatic, mysterious with a distinctive augmented 2nd interval

theory.mode: Not a mode of major scale - independent scale family derived from natural minor with raised 7th

relativeScale.name: Major Scale
relativeScale.intervalDistance: Minor 3rd up from harmonic minor root (A Harmonic Minor relates to C Major key signature)

keyExamples.notes: A - B - C - D - E - F - G# - A
keyExamples.commonUse: Most common harmonic minor key on guitar, open position friendly

keyExamples.notes: E - F# - G - A - B - C - D# - E
keyExamples.commonUse: Natural guitar key, open position with dramatic character

keyExamples.notes: B - C# - D - E - F# - G - A# - B
keyExamples.commonUse: Higher position lead work, neoclassical metal favorite

keyExamples.notes: C - D - E♭ - F - G - A♭ - B - C
keyExamples.keySignature: 3 flats (E♭, A♭, B♭) with B natural
keyExamples.commonUse: Classical position, common in classical and film score writing

patterns.description: Natural guitar key with open strings. Root on 5th string, features the dramatic augmented 2nd between F and G#.
patterns.fretDiagram: Uses open strings and first 4 frets, strings 5-2

patterns.description: Another natural guitar key starting from open 6th string, full range position
patterns.fretDiagram: Uses open strings and first 4 frets, strings 6-4

patterns.description: Higher position for lead work and soloing, moveable pattern for all keys

commonPositions.usage: Classical guitar, fundamental harmonic minor shapes
Metal riffs, dramatic open position playing
Neoclassical lead work, upper register solos

diatonicChords.function: Tonic - Home chord, dramatic minor center
Mediant - Augmented triad, exotic color from the raised 7th
Dominant - Major dominant chord (THE key feature of harmonic minor), strong V-i resolution
Submediant - Major chord providing contrast and color
Leading tone - Strong pull to tonic, dramatic resolution

commonProgressions.name: Classical Cadence (V-i)
commonProgressions.description: The fundamental harmonic minor cadence - the raised 7th creates a major V chord that resolves powerfully to the minor tonic

commonProgressions.name: Minor Cadence (i-iv-V-i)
commonProgressions.description: Full harmonic minor cadence with subdominant approach, the backbone of classical minor key harmony

commonProgressions.name: Andalusian Cadence (i-♭VII-♭VI-V)
commonProgressions.description: Descending bass line progression with dramatic resolution through the major V chord, common in Flamenco and Spanish music

commonProgressions.name: Neoclassical Progression (i-♭VI-iv-V)
commonProgressions.description: Common in neoclassical metal and film scores, builds dramatic tension before dominant resolution

genreApplications.usage: Foundation of classical minor key harmony, essential for V7-i resolutions
examples: Bach - Invention No. 4 in D minor

genreApplications.usage: Neoclassical metal solos and dark, dramatic riffs and compositions
Middle Eastern, Spanish, and Eastern European folk traditions share harmonic minor's exotic character
Creates suspense, darkness, and dramatic tension in horror and drama soundtracks
Complex harmonic structures combining classical influences with metal power

practiceExercises.name: A Harmonic Minor Scale Runs
practiceExercises.description: Practice the A harmonic minor scale ascending and descending with emphasis on the augmented 2nd interval between F and G#
instructions: Start slowly with metronome at 60 BPM
Pay special attention to the augmented 2nd between F and G#
Practice both alternate and economy picking
Gradually increase tempo as accuracy improves

practiceExercises.name: Augmented 2nd Interval Focus
practiceExercises.description: Isolate and practice the characteristic augmented 2nd interval that defines the harmonic minor sound
instructions: Play the F to G# interval repeatedly to internalize the sound
Approach the augmented 2nd from different scale degrees
Focus on clean intonation and smooth transitions
Practice singing the interval to develop ear recognition

practiceExercises.name: Classical Arpeggio Patterns
practiceExercises.description: Practice broken chord patterns in harmonic minor for classical and neoclassical applications
instructions: Practice each arpeggio pattern separately first
Work on different arpeggio directions (ascending, descending, mixed)
Apply to Am-Dm-E-Am progression for musical context

practiceExercises.name: Harmonic Minor Ear Training
practiceExercises.description: Compare harmonic minor with natural minor to hear the characteristic raised 7th and exotic augmented 2nd
instructions: Play harmonic minor, then natural minor back to back
Focus on the 7th degree difference (G# vs G natural in A minor)
Listen for the exotic augmented 2nd between the 6th and 7th degrees
Practice identifying harmonic minor in classical and metal recordings

relatedScales.differences: Harmonic minor has a natural 7th (raised) instead of flat 7th - creates the leading tone
relatedScales.usage: Softer, more traditional minor sound without the exotic augmented 2nd

relatedScales.differences: Melodic minor raises both the 6th and 7th degrees, eliminating the augmented 2nd
relatedScales.usage: Smoother melodic motion, commonly used ascending in classical and throughout in jazz

relatedScales.differences: Phrygian dominant is built on the 5th degree of harmonic minor, sharing its exotic character
relatedScales.usage: Spanish/flamenco character, Middle Eastern music, metal

relatedScales.differences: Hungarian minor has a raised 4th in addition to the raised 7th, creating two augmented 2nds
relatedScales.usage: Even more exotic character, Eastern European and Romani music traditions

relatedScales.differences: Symmetrical 8-note scale vs 7-note harmonic minor; both generate diminished harmony
relatedScales.usage: Jazz and classical diminished chord contexts, more symmetrical approach

prerequisites: Understanding of intervals and half/whole steps
nextSteps: Phrygian dominant mode (5th mode of harmonic minor)

practiceRoutine.focus: Multiple positions and the augmented 2nd interval
Musical application in classical and metal contexts
